name: AlertDialog
description:
A confirmation for destructive or irreversible actions. Cancel takes focus first; Esc
cancels; outside presses do nothing. While the action runs, it cannot be dismissed.
signature: ({ trigger, open: openProp, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, onOpenChangeComplete, title, description, confirmLabel, cancelLabel, pendingLabel, tone, icon, onConfirm, failureTitle, }: AlertDialogProps): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: Visible label for cancelling or dismissing the request.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: A verb naming the outcome: "Remove device".

props.name: description
props.description: One factual sentence: what happens, and whether it can be undone.

props.name: failureTitle
props.description: Title of the failure toast. Default: "<confirmLabel> failed".

props.name: icon
props.description: An icon element without an explicit size; the component sizes it through its tokens.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description:
Runs in place: the confirm button shows pending, then ✓ and the dialog closes. If it
throws, the button shakes ✕, the dialog stays open and the reason goes to a toast.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state when the trigger opens it, Cancel or Esc dismisses it, or it closes after `onConfirm` succeeds. Not called for dismissals while the action runs. Pair with `open` to control it.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Called with the final open state once the open or close animation has finished.

props.name: open
props.description: Controls whether the overlay is open.

props.name: pendingLabel
props.description: Label shown while the asynchronous action runs. Its width is reserved with the other feedback labels.

props.name: title
props.description: Names the target: "Remove NST-C106 from Northstar Studio?" (R12.4).

props.name: tone
props.description: The semantic tone. Use danger and warning for consequences and states.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens it. Omit when controlling `open`.
